notes: Independent review of PR #13, scoped to the two things not previously covered: whether the reviewed_commit binding works, and whether decisions D9-D14 are a faithful record. The mission text and quality floor were reviewed across four earlier rounds on the predecessor branch and were not re-reviewed here. BINDING VERIFIED BY TESTING, not by reading: a record with no reviewed_commit is rejected; a mismatched sha is rejected as STALE with both shas named; full-sha and 7-character-prefix matches pass; reviewed_commit values of a single character and of an empty string are both rejected because a minimum length of 7 is enforced in code independently of the schema pattern; a stale-only record yields zero independent reviews rather than a reduced count; and resolve_head_sha returns None rather than throwing or silently passing when a ref cannot be resolved, with the run still failing. DECISIONS VERIFIED against the repository rather than against the decision text: core has exactly one Codex mention, a comment at core/lwb_core/__init__.py:8, with no import and no branch; removing Codex would stop exactly nine tests, seven in tests/adapters/test_codex_hook_io.py and two in tests/conformance/, which import the adapter directly, while the lane-classification tests only reference codex as a string and were correctly excluded from that count; D12's arithmetic of eight adoptable plus three caveated plus four to build totals fifteen; the D1, D5 and D6 amendments append rather than overwrite, leaving the original text intact; and no decision contradicts another or the mission. The RTK removal claim was checked against live disk rather than the session-start snapshot, which predated the cleanup. NOT VERIFIED: the claim that caveman's compress skill runs only on explicit invocation concerns global environment state outside this repository and could not be checked mechanically here. THIS REVIEW RETURNED DISAGREE ON ITS FIRST PASS, and that blocker is recorded rather than hidden: the binding as originally written was unsatisfiable, because committing a review record advances the head past the sha the record names, so no committed record could ever match. That is the same defect class as two earlier gates here -- a check that cannot pass. It was fixed by excluding record-only commits under reviews/ and proof/ when computing the head a record is compared against. KNOWN LIMIT per D10: the owner is the approver and these identity strings are self-attested; this is an audit trail, not proof that two sessions existed. FINAL ROUND, on commit d3eb1d6: the reviewed_commit gate was itself unsatisfiable when first written, because committing a review record advances the head past the sha that record names. The fix excludes record-only commits — those touching nothing outside reviews/ and proof/ — when computing the head a record is compared against. Verified by building a throwaway repository rather than by reading: a trailing reviews-only or proof-only commit is correctly skipped; a record naming an older SUBSTANTIVE commit is still rejected as STALE, so the original protection survives; a mixed commit touching both reviews/ and scripts/ is correctly treated as substantive; an empty commit does not slip through the all-empty case; and a decoy path reviews_evil/x does not match because the check requires the literal slash. Termination confirmed: one bounded walk over git log, returning at the first non-record-only commit, so committing a record naming the current substantive head leaves the head unchanged on the next run. NOT CHECKED: behaviour under detached-HEAD or shallow-clone CI checkouts, and whether commits_in_range interacts with record-only commits inside the PR range.
